item.description: Why federal systems should begin migrating now: the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat, NIST FIPS 203/204/205 standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), cryptographic agility, and a phased hybrid transition. A Ravonics architectural primer.

item.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Architecture for Federal Systems | Ravonics
item.description: A technical architecture guide to implementing NIST PQC standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA) across federal communications and data-at-rest: crypto-agility design, hybrid modes, key management, and phased migration sequencing.

item.title: The Quantum Threat: Why Federal Systems Should Begin PQC Migration Now | Ravonics
item.description: The harvest-now-decrypt-later threat, CRQC timeline uncertainty, NIST FIPS 203/204/205, NSA CNSA 2.0 transition timelines, and OMB/NSM-10 guidance: why federal agencies must begin post-quantum cryptography migration now, not after a quantum computer arrives.

item.title: Autonomous Swarm Coordination | Architecture Concepts | Ravonics

item.title: Zero Trust Implementation for Federal Networks | Ravonics
item.description: A practical framework for zero trust in federal environments: identity, micro-segmentation, continuous verification, and policy-as-code aligned to NIST SP 800-207, with immutable infrastructure and GitOps as enablers. A Ravonics perspective.

item.title: Zero Trust Architecture: Why Mandates Stall Without Architectural Foundation | Ravonics
item.description: OMB M-22-09 and CISA ZTMM mandate zero trust adoption across federal agencies, yet most programs stall. This perspective examines why identity and ICAM foundation must come first, and the architectural patterns that make zero trust adoption practical rather than performative.
